label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
@Kavya, I've seen your post, and I know a lot of people in our Foundry91 cohort have read it as being about DabbaDost. It is. So I'd rather speak for myself than let the comments do it.

First, the part I got wrong. Two engineers from SitterNest joined us on 3 Nov. I knew where they worked from the first conversation. I should have called you before we made the offers. I only reached out after. That's on me, and I'm sorry. You deserved to hear it from me first, not from your team.

Now a few things I need to set straight, because people are already repeating them:

We didn't DM anyone. We put up a backend dev opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 Sept, open to anyone. The first person applied on his own on 19 Sept. The second came two weeks later as his referral.

The hike was 22% over their current CTC, not 40%. I'm putting the real number here only because 40 is going around and it isn't true.

We didn't promise ESOPs we don't have. Our pool is small, but it exists and has been on paper since January.

I'm not sharing anything about the two of them beyond this. They didn't ask to be part of this, and I'd request everyone tagging and guessing to please leave them out of it.

Some context on why this one hurts. Before demo day in March, you sat with me in the Koramangala office till 1am fixing our Razorpay webhook mess. You didn't have to. I haven't forgotten it, and I won't. This post isn't me picking a fight with you. I respect you and what you're building.

I also think this will keep happening. We are 11 startups hiring from the same small pool of people in HSR and Koramangala. Good engineers will move between our companies, and they should be free to. But how we founders handle it is in our hands.

So here's a simple rule I'd like to propose for cohort 4, and I'll follow it first: if you're interviewing someone from another batch company, you give that founder a heads up before you make the offer. Not permission, just a heads up. A phone call. It costs nothing and it would have saved both of us this week.

Kavya, I messaged you after the second offer was accepted, and I understand why you didn't reply. My door's open: coffee or a call, this week, whenever you're okay.

---

This is about 420 words and roughly 2,450 characters, so it's within both limits. Swap "@Kavya" for her actual tag when you post it.
